To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
VSV-fused hybridoma cell lines produce more IgG than other types of hybridoma cells.
vesicular stomatitis (VSV) virus-mediated cell fusion preferentially generated IgG-producing hybridoma cells.
vesicular stomatitis (VSV) fusion preferentially generates IgG-producing hybridoma clones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the generation of hybridoma clones secreting monoclonal antibodies, using vesicular stomatitis viruses (VSV) as fusion agent.
the development of a new technique for the generation of monoclonals, and we believe it will be of great interest to the scientific community.
the generation and characterization of monoclonal antibodies against the major capsid protein of the human papillomavirus (HPV) 16.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for production of IgM antibodies, SV-fusion is the best choice, for IgG antibodies, VSV-fused is the best choice.
VSV-fused hybridomas are more efficient for the production of IgG MAbs than PEG-fused ones.
VSV-mediated cell fusion is a promising technique for production of Ig-producing hybridomas, especially IgG-producers, and is a good alternative to the PEG-mediated fusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

VSV-fused hybridomas have the following characteristics; (a) high frequency of IgG producers, (b) high frequency of secreting high titres of antibodies, (c) high frequency of producing antibodies against antigens which are not recognized by the parental myeloma cells, (d) high frequency of hybridomas with high growth rate, (e) low frequency of producing IgM antibodies, and (f) low frequency of secreting low titres of antibodies.
VSV-fused hybridomas are superior to PEG-fused hybridomas in the production of monoclonal antibodies, particularly IgG antibodies.
the use of VSV-fused cells is a useful alternative method for the production of monoclonal antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

vesicular stomatitis viruses (VSV) are an effective tool for the generation of hybridomas, and that the use of VSV can be a valuable addition to the arsenal of tools for generating monoclonal antibodies.
vesicular stomatitis viruses can be used as a tool to generate monoclonals.
VSV fusion has a higher frequency of IgG-producing hybridoma than PEG fusion.
